ctx.x: Lily and I had decided to buy a second hand car. Albert Nicholas had a Volkswagen "Coccinelle" which had once belonged to Kenny Clarke and as Nick wasn't working very much at that time, he wanted to sell it. Neither of us could drive but we decided to take lessons in Juan-les-Pins. We asked Albert if we would accept to drive us there and we would pay his expenses and his fare back.

So the 29th of June we left Paris with a big load of luggage, our cockatoo named Coco and our Persian cat, Princess. Both animals were scared to death in that car and Coco was repeating non stop "bonjour Coco, ca va Coco?" Princess was mewing. Albert was driving at the speed of 50 miles an hour. We tried to find an hotel room in different places but all the hotels were packed so we had to make the trip non stop except for meals. When we arrived on the Cote d'Azur, Nick was so tired that he was falling asleep on…

We had a very good friend, Leopold de Lima e Silva who was the son of Mistinguett, the famous Music Hall star. Leopold had inherited from his mother a very nice house with a big garden. It was called the Bungalow and was situated at the Cap d'Antibes, between Antibes and Juan-les-Pins, a 10 minute walk to the "Vieux Colombier". The house was separated in two flats, one was empty and Leopold had proposed to us to live there for a very mild rent and of course we had accepted with joy.
